headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist: TREK’s MCP/browser stack can ingest and act on social-auto-upload outputs, while both touch sensitive account data and secrets.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: TREK uses MCP and browsers, so it can ingest content from social-auto-upload outputs if those outputs are bridged into its workflow; social-auto-upload also handles files and account data. No shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than proven, but the interaction is plausible enough to exceed low severity.
conditions: IF social-auto-upload output is copied into TREK via MCP, browser automation, or shared files
IF TREK treats imported content as instructions or task text without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable any automatic import of generated captions or notes
Require provenance labels on all cross-agent text
Use a manual review step before TREK consumes agent A output
Restrict MCP tools to read-only sources
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping at the bridge

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches account data and media files, while agent B touches reservations, email addresses, API keys, and MFA secrets. Both are open-source docs-only profiles with file surfaces, but no shared workspace is documented. The pair still presents a plausible leakage path if operators place them in the same directory or sync their outputs.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or synced upload directory
IF TREK logs or exports content that includes secrets or reservation data
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories
Move secrets out of any shared upload path
Rotate any exposed API keys or MFA secrets after testing
Review TREK logs for sensitive fields before retention
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, while agent B can use MCP and browsers but no filesystem write is documented. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The main overlap is read/interaction on shared resources, so the blast radius is limited unless an undocumented write path exists.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same mutable resource
IF TREK’s MCP tools are configured to mutate shared state
mitigations: Keep both agents on separate accounts
Avoid shared mutable directories
Disable write-capable MCP tools for TREK
Use lockfiles or single-writer scheduling
requires-engineering: add resource-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK is a real-time collaborative planner with AI built in and browser/MCP tooling, so it can plausibly treat social-auto-upload outputs as authoritative inputs and then act on them. Social-auto-upload produces upload-related content and account data, creating a pathway where one agent’s output drives the other’s downstream actions without verification. Uncertainty about the exact bridge pushes this to high rather than medium.
conditions: IF TREK ingests captions, metadata, or task text generated by social-auto-upload
IF TREK executes bookings, edits, or other actions based on unverified imported content
mitigations: Require human approval before any downstream action
Add a verification step for imported facts and dates
Mark imported text as untrusted by default
Limit TREK to draft-only mode for cross-agent inputs
requires-engineering: implement source-aware validation

E_compliance.rationale: Agent B handles highly sensitive travel data including API keys, MFA secrets, and reservations, while agent A handles account data and media. Both are open-source and docs-only, but TREK’s self-hosted collaborative setup and logging/files suggest retention and residency controls may differ from social-auto-upload’s simpler upload workflow. The mismatch is plausible, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF the same personal travel data is routed through both agents
IF TREK logs or retains secrets longer than the operator expects
mitigations: Compare retention settings before use
Exclude secrets from shared workflows
Purge logs after testing
Document data residency for each agent
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies
